text: Data parallelism (DP) gives every GPU a different slice of the mini-batch and averages the gradients, but it replicates the full model state on every GPU, so it does not reduce memory per device at all: plain DP (PyTorch's DistributedDataParallel, DDP) runs out of memory beyond about 1.4B parameters on 32 GB V100s, however many GPUs you add ( §1 ).

text: The idea: ZeRO-DP, data parallelism without the redundancy §4.1, §5, Figure 1 Three observations drive the design ( §4.1 ): (a) DP scales better than MP because it keeps large, efficient matrix multiplies and communicates less; (b) DP wastes memory because every process stores identical model states, while MP partitions them; (c) both keep every state for the whole step, although a layer's parameters, for example, are only needed during that layer's forward and backward.
